jobs.description: Apply now to join FAU, where tomorrow begins. For more information on everything FAU has to offer, please visit www.fau.edu/jobs . Note: Current FAU employees must apply as an internal applicant by logging into their existing Workday employee account. Position Summary: The Department of Surgery at Florida Atlantic University (FAU) seeks a full-time academic surgeon who is board certified/eligible in General Surgery and Surgical Critical Care. The primary responsibility of this position is to serve as a Surgical Critical Care physician, providing comprehensive management of critically ill surgical patients in the intensive care unit. The faculty member will also participate in General Surgery call and have a significant role in the education, supervision, and mentorship of FAU General Surgery residents. The faculty member will report directly to the Chair of the Department of Surgery and work collaboratively with the General Surgery Residency Program Director and Department leadership. Responsibilities Serve primarily as a Surgical Critical Care/ICU attending, providing approximately 14–16 daytime ICU shifts per month, generally 12-hour shifts. Direct daily multidisciplinary ICU rounds and management of critically ill postoperative and surgical patients. Manage complex critical care conditions including respiratory failure, mechanical ventilation, sepsis and septic shock, hemodynamic instability, multiorgan failure, acute kidney injury, nutritional and metabolic disorders, and complex postoperative complications. Perform appropriate critical care procedures within clinical privileges, including airway management, central venous and arterial catheter placement, and other bedside procedures. Provide critical care consultation and coordinate care with surgical and multidisciplinary teams. Participate in ICU quality improvement, patient safety, and morbidity and mortality activities. Participate in approximately 4–5 General Surgery call assignments per month, including evaluation and management of acute surgical conditions, inpatient consultation, operative care, and perioperative management. This is not a trauma surgery position; trauma surgery will not be a primary clinical responsibility. Provide direct supervision and bedside teaching of General Surgery residents in the ICU and during General Surgery call. Participate in resident evaluations, curriculum development, didactic conferences, M&M conferences, journal clubs, case conferences, and other educational activities. Maintain an educational environment consistent with ACGME and FAU standards. The successful candidate will receive an academic faculty appointment in the Florida Atlantic University Charles E. Schmidt College of Medicine, Department of Surgery, with academic rank commensurate with qualifications and experience. Minimum Qualifications: • MD or DO degree from an accredited medical school. • Completion of an ACGME-accredited General Surgery residency. • Board certification/eligibility in General Surgery. • Fellowship training and board certification/eligibility in Surgical Critical Care. • Eligibility for an unrestricted Florida medical license and appropriate clinical privileges. • Demonstrated commitment to academic medicine, graduate medical education, teaching, and resident mentorship. Salary: Commensurate with qualifications and experience. College or Department: Charles E. Schmidt College of Medicine Location: Clinical - Off Campus Location (COM use only) Work Days and Hours: N/A Application Deadline: 2026-12-31 Special Instructions to Applicant: This position is open until filled and may close without prior notice. This position is subject to funding. jobs.description: The Nathan M. Bisk College of Business at Florida Institute of Technology is seeking a unique academic scholar to join our team in transforming the way business education is delivered. We invite applications from enthusiastic, highly engaged faculty for an adjunct position in Business Ethics. The Nathan M. Bisk College of Business at Florida Institute of Technology is seeking a unique academic scholar to join our team in transforming the way business education is delivered. We invite applications from enthusiastic, highly engaged faculty for an adjunct position in Leadership & Management. The candidate must be academically qualified at the undergraduate and master's degree levels. Candidates must have a graduate degree in business as a minimum. The position requires teaching skills in the field of leadership and management. The Bisk College of Business is currently accredited through the International Accreditation Council for Business Education (IACBE) and is a member of the Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB). Equal Opportunity Florida Institute of Technology does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, national or ethnic origin, religion, disability, age, genetic information, marital status, citizenship status, veteran status, and other legally protected characteristics in its activities and programs. In accordance with Title IX of the Education Amendments of 1972, Florida Tech does not discriminate on the basis of sex. Inquiries concerning the application of the Non-Discrimination and Anti-Harassment policy may be directed to the Equal Opportunity Director and Investigator at 150 West University Blvd, Melbourne, FL 32901, or email equalopp@fit.edu , or +1 321-674-7153; or to the U.S. Department of Education Office for Civil Rights. Americans with Disabilities Act Please notify us at least five days in advance if a reasonable accommodation for a disability is needed by calling the Office of Human Resources at 321-674-8100. Annual Security & Fire Safety Report The federal Jeanne Clery Disclosure of Campus Security Policy and Campus Crime Statistics Act (Clery Act) requires colleges and universities, both public and private, participating in federal student aid programs to disclose campus safety information, and imposes certain basic requirements for handling incidents of sexual violence and emergency situations. Florida Tech’s 2026 Annual Security and Fire Safety Report includes statistics for the previous three years concerning reported crimes that occurred on campus; in certain off-campus buildings or property owned or controlled by Florida Tech; and on public property within, or immediately adjacent to and accessible from, the campus. The numbers provided include crime statistics that were reported to local law enforcement agencies, campus security and other Campus Security Authorities. The report also includes institutional policy statements regarding campus safety and security measures; descriptions of prevention and awareness programs; related university procedures and important guidance; and other essential safety information. You can obtain a printed copy of this report at the Department of Security Welcome Center located at 3126 Panther Place, during normal business hours, or by accessing the following web site 2026 Annual Security and Fire Safety Report . Official Transcripts Official transcripts of all collegiate work must be sent directly from the attended institution to the Office of Human Resources prior to the first day of employment. All international degrees must have a course-by-course official evaluation and translation sent to the Human Resources Office directly from an evaluation company affiliated with the National Association of Credential Evaluation Services, Inc. (NACES). We are an E-verify employer

jobs.title: Adjunct Faculty - EDES 330X: Costume Design & Digital Visualization
jobs.college: Ringling College of Art and Design
jobs.description: APPLICATION INSTRUCTIONS: Current Ringling Employees - Apply for jobs internally using the Workday "Jobs Hub" App from Global Navigation Menu on Workday Home Page. External Applicants - Click the "Apply" button to complete the external application. Job Description Summary Adjunct Faculty - EDES 330X: Costume Design & Digital Visualization Job Description EDES 330X: Costume Design & Digital Visualization Course description: Through the creation of original costume designs, students explore storytelling, character development, and digital visualization. The course guides students through the contemporary costume design process, from early visual research and concept sketches to textile design, technical communication, 3D garment creation, and photorealistic rendering. Course goals subject to adjustment by instructor: Using industry-standard digital tools and workflows, students develop practical skills in visualizing and presenting costume concepts for theatre and film, themed entertainment, fashion, and emerging immersive media. This position is available for remote work in FL. Course Goals: Develop an integrated approach to costume design that connects storytelling, character development, and visual communication within a digital workflow. Build research skills that support concept development, world-building, and informed design decision-making. Develop fluency in digital tools and workflows used for textile creation, garment construction exploration, and costume visualization. Strengthen understanding of form, silhouette, and material behavior through iterative 3D exploration and refinement. Develop effective visual communication skills for presenting design in professional critique and presentation contexts. Education and Experience Minimum Qualifications: A master’s degree that demonstrates expertise appropriate for teaching a course/s listed in this announcement OR a 4-year professional degree (BFA) in art or design and equivalent expertise, training and experience, with an appropriate record of professional creative achievement. Professional portfolio demonstrating skills and experience in the curricular area. A repertoire of engaging teaching techniques that reaches out to a variety of learning styles. Familiarity with digital technologies in teaching. Preferred Qualifications: A terminal degree in art, design, theater. Entertainment Industry Experience with costuming. College level teaching experience. Significant professional creative practice. Special Instructions to Applicants: Required materials include cover letter, resume or CV, employment and education history, contact information of three references (names, titles, email, and telephone numbers), examples of personal work, and, an unofficial transcript copy of the most relevant degree. Student work examples may also be submitted. Candidates may be asked to submit additional materials if needed. Official transcripts will be required upon hire. For portfolio, you have the option to upload electronic documents/images, up to 5 MB, or a URL . Review of materials will begin immediately. Applications to this pool will be reviewed throughout the year as positions become available and until all vacancies are filled. Courses may be added as needed – please check for revisions. Inquiries: aamail@ringling.edu Ringling College of Art and Design is an Equal Opportunity Employer. The College provides equal employment opportunity to all persons without regard to sex, age, gender, color, race, national or ethnic origin, religion, marital status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, disability, veteran status, genetic information, or any other basis prohibited by law.

jobs.title: Adjunct Faculty - MATH 250X: Math for Motion
jobs.college: Ringling College of Art and Design
jobs.description: APPLICATION INSTRUCTIONS: Current Ringling Employees - Apply for jobs internally using the Workday "Jobs Hub" App from Global Navigation Menu on Workday Home Page. External Applicants - Click the "Apply" button to complete the external application. Job Description Summary Job Description MATH 250X: MATH FOR MOTION Course description: This course explores linear systems and vectors, coordinates and spatial reasoning, and trigonometry for motion, interpolation, and time-based systems. Calculus experience not required. Course goals subject to adjustment by instructor: Students will learn fundamental vector math, basic linear algebra, and trigonometry. Students will also be introduced to coordinate systems and spatial reasoning; matrix math for transforms and hierarchy; relative versus absolute transforms; rotation order and issues like gimbal lock; and related mathematics to assist in visualizing and solving problems in real-time applications. Minimum five (5) years of recent commercial driving experience is required Minimum three (3) years of experience training or supervising commercial drivers is preferred. Current DOT Medical Examiner's Certificate (or ability to obtain).

jobs.title: Adjunct Faculty, Epidemiology
jobs.description: Barry University’s Biomedical Sciences (BMS) Master of Science Program in the College of Health and Wellness is currently seeking an individual who will teach Epidemiology at the graduate level to students in the BMS degree program. The BMS Epidemiology course is offered in a HyFlex format. The faculty member teaches the class as scheduled from a classroom at the BMS Hollywood campus while simultaneously teaching to online students who are synchronously logged in through MS Teams to participate with the classroom lecture. The adjunct faculty member will collaborate with other faculty within and outside of the department in the development and execution of this course. Steeped in a tradition of rigor, the BMS program prepare students who wish to advance as health care professionals or biomedical scientists. The BMS curriculum serves to strengthen a student’s application for medical, dental or other professional health education by delivering a sequence of core science courses similar to the first-year of a medical, dental, podiatric, or other professional school curriculum in biomedical sciences. The program is designed to provide motivated students with an intensive and unique learning experience. Preparation of class materials to teach a graduate level course in Epidemiology to students in the BMS graduate program. Utilization of Canvas, Teams, and ExamSoft to manage and deliver the BMS Epidemiology course. Delivery of graduate level lectures and teaching in a HyFlex format. BMS Epidemiology is a 3-credit hour course that meets in a hybrid environment (online students attend synchronously) once a week for 3 hours. Assessment and grading of students enrolled in the Epidemiology course—submission of grades at the end of the semester Qualifications/Requirements - 1-3 years of experience - PhD in Biomedical Sciences or related field with pertinent specific training in or related to Epidemiology; OR MD/DO professional medical degree - Previous experience teaching pathology concepts - Advanced experience with the p reparation of lectures, assignments, and exam materials for teaching purposes Benefits: Barry University offers a comprehensive benefits package to full-time employees that includes health, dental, vision, life insurance, retirement, tuition assistance, paid time off and work/life balance initiatives such as wellness programs, spirituality in the workplace, and training and development. Barry University is an Equal Opportunity Employer, committed to a diverse and inclusive work environment.

jobs.title: Adjunct Faculty, Mathematical Sciences
jobs.description: Summary The Department of Math and Computer Science is one of 11 departments in the College of Arts & Sciences. The Department offers Bachelor of Science degrees in Mathematics, Computer Science, and Computer Information Sciences. All majors must choose a specialization in Data Analytics, Cybersecurity, or Digital Media. The Department of Mathematics and Computer Science at Barry University invites applications for part-time adjunct faculty members in the area of Mathematical Sciences. The positions emphasize excellence in undergraduate instruction in alignment with Barry University’s core commitments to social justice, collaborative learning, and inclusive education. Selected candidates will be responsible for teaching undergraduate courses including College Algebra, Precalculus, and Elementary Probability and Statistics. Contracts are offered on a semester-by-semester basis depending on departmental and enrollment needs. Essential Functions Teach undergraduate courses in Mathematical Sciences, including but not limited to: - College Algebra - Precalculus - Elementary Probability and Statistics Follow established syllabi and collaborate with full-time faculty to ensure learning outcomes are met. Maintain office hours for out-of-class student support. jobs.description: Summary Barry University’s Department of Counseling & School Psychology in the School of Mental Health provides a quality education in a caring environment for the adult student population. The Adjunct Faculty member will teach courses within the School Psychology master’s and specialist degree programs located on the main campus of Barry University in Miami. The School Psychology Program follows the scientist-practitioner model and is accredited by the National Association of School Psychologists and is approved by the Florida Department of Education. We are currently seeking adjunct faculty to add to our roster of contract faculty for assignments on an as-needed basis for the following Graduate Programs: School Psychology (MS and SSP) Courses are delivered in several formats, including face-to-face and online; terms are seven (summer courses) and 16 weeks in length (fall and spring). Graduate courses meet once per week (Monday-Thursday) for three hours for the entire semester, with start times from 5:30 to 6:30. Adjuncts are responsible for consulting with their respective Program Directors in the development and execution of the course, as well as additional responsibilities outlined in the faculty handbook Qualifications/Requirements Minimum degree is a Specialist's degree in School Psychology; doctoral degree preferred. Applied experience in the field is required. Prior college-level teaching experience with an adult student population is preferred. Applicants should be comfortable using computer technology appropriate for graduate-level university courses and professional scoring platforms used by school psychologists. jobs.description: Employment App Help APPLICATION INSTRUCTIONS Do not use Internet Explorer to complete the application process. The portal used for this program is not supported by Explorer. To successfully complete the online application and submit documents the following internet browsers are supported: Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, and Firefox. Applicants are advised to select the option to retrieve an employment application KEY by using the Save and Finish later button on the first page of the application so that they may save changes and retrieve their work later. If technical difficulties are experienced while completing the application process, applicants can use the key to log back into their application and complete the process. A separate application must be made for each individual position of interest. Materials from former position applications can not be transferred to an application for another position. Cover letters and letters of interest may be addressed to the Hiring Committee if not otherwise instructed in the job posting. Once the application form is submitted and supporting materials are uploaded additional changes cannot be made. Applicants can resubmit their application materials for the same position by completing another online application form and submitting more documents which will be added to the original application. However, the original documents will remain with the original submission. After selecting "Submit" at the end of the application form, applicants will be able to upload up to 4 additional documents in upload fields labeled "supporting document". Multiple documents can be scanned together as one document and uploaded using one of the 4 upload fields. For example a CV, teaching philosophy statement, and transcripts can be scanned together as one document and uploaded using the "supporting document" field. Attachments can be accepted in Word document or PDF format only. However, the original documents will remain with the original submission. After selecting "Submit" at the end of the application form, applicants will be able to upload up to 4 additional documents in upload fields labeled "supporting document". Attachments can be accepted in Word document or PDF format only. Document file names must not have special characters, including punctuation marks such as a period or dot, as this prevents the file from uploading with the application form. The online application system will generate an automatic confirmation e-mail to the applicant when the application is successfully submitted. This is the only confirmation provided by the College. Position Number: Adjunct Instructor Pool - Respiratory TherapyClassification Title: InstructorWorking Title: Adjunct InstructorDepartment: Health Sciences and AdministrationFLSA Status: ExemptSalary Range: Dependent on Course and CredentialsPay Basis: Annually POSITION OVERVIEW JOB SUMMARY: Part-time adjunct instructors in the Bachelor of Science in Respiratory Therapy (BSRT) program within the Department of Health Sciences and Administration deliver high-quality instruction across didactic, laboratory, and/or clinical courses. Key responsibilities include providing evidence-based teaching, evaluating student performance, fostering a supportive learning environment, and ensuring alignment with course outcomes and accreditation standards. Adjunct instructors work collaboratively with full-time faculty and participate in required training and course meetings to promote student success and maintain overall program quality.The Bachelor of Science in Respiratory Therapy (BSRT) program is accredited by the Commission on Accreditation for Respiratory Care (CoARC). MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS: Candidates must meet the following minimum qualifications to be considered:- Earned a Master’s degree in Respiratory Care or closely related discipline from a CoARC-accredited respiratory therapy program. - Valid NBRC Registered Respiratory Therapist (RRT) credential.- Active Respiratory Care License in the state of Florida in good standing.- Relevant respiratory therapy experience, including clinical, academic, and/or managerial roles. PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS: Preferred candidates will hold a doctorate degree in an appropriate field of specialization or a closely related discipline from an accredited institution, beyond the required respiratory care degree.Prior teaching experience in respiratory therapy or related health sciences in online or hybrid teaching formats.1 year or more experience in areas such as mechanical ventilation, critical care, neonatal/pediatric care, or cardiopulmonary diagnostics; and familiarity with CoARC standards and competency-based education. Advanced credentials Adult Critical Care Specialty (ACCS), Neonatal/Pediatric Specialty (NPS), or Sleep Disorders Specialty CRT-SDS/RRT-SDS) and active involvement in professional organizations such as the American Association for Respiratory Care (AARC) , Florida Society Respiratory Care (FSRC), or related specialty societies. Special Requirements or Considerations of the Job: This position requires a criminal background screen. This position requires licensure, certification, or other qualifications described in the Special Instructions. Special Instructions to Applicants: All applicants will need to upload their current CV and copies of their NBRC Registered Respiratory Therapist (RRT) credential and Florida Respiratory Care License.Candidates must apply online through the University of West Florida website: https://careers.uwf.edu. Applicants are required to attach a CV, letter of interest and contact information for two professional references. References will be contacted upon submission of this application. An opportunity to upload these documents will be provided during the application process. For assistance, please contact Human Resources at 850-474-2694 or email jobs@uwf.edu.The college is building a pool of adjuncts for teaching opportunities for upcoming semesters. Applications will be accepted on an on-going basis. Your application will be reviewed by the Department of Health Sciences and Administration. jobs.title: Adjunct Instructor, High School EMT
jobs.description: The High School EMT Instructor is responsible for delivering high-quality EMT instruction to high school students enrolled in this specialized high school program. This position ensures that students gain the necessary knowledge and skills to meet state and national EMT certification requirements. The instructor follows established curriculum guidelines, maintains compliance with accreditation standards, and supports student success through mentorship and hands-on training. This role requires collaboration with the High School Program Coordinator, the High School faculty, and clinical partners to create a comprehensive learning environment All Barry EMS (EMT and Paramedic) Instructors ensures that course delivery adheres to Florida BEMS 64J standards and NATIONAL STANDARDS EMT and Paramedic Scope of Practice . EMT Instructors shall maintain accurate records of student attendance, progress, and certification eligibility in compliance with program policies. Instructors be well versed in the delivery of EMT course content with the end goal of properly preparing students for NREMT licensure examination The High School EMT Instructor is the primary person who I responsible for preparing students for emergency service entry point. This position requires strong leadership, adaptability, and enthusiasm for EMS education. Instructors works closely with the High School Program Coordinator, and industry professionals to ensure students are fully equipped with the knowledge required to succeed in their EMT careers. Instruction and Classroom Management: Deliver EMT course instruction aligned with state and national standards, utilizing both classroom-based and hands-on training methods. Foster an engaging and supportive learning environment while ensuring students develop competency in essential EMT skills and knowledge. Maintain classroom discipline and encourage student participation. Clinical and Lab Training: Oversee and facilitate practical skill labs and simulations, ensuring students develop proficiency in patient assessment, life-saving interventions, and pre-hospital emergency care. Monitor and evaluate student performance during hands-on exercises.20 Student Assessment and Evaluation: Develop and administer quizzes, exams, and practical skill evaluations to assess student progress. Provide constructive feedback and additional instruction as needed to ensure student comprehension and skill mastery. Be accountable for final student test scores and student NREMT certification. Compliance and Accreditation Support: Maintain accurate records of student attendance, progress, and certification eligibility in compliance with program policies. Student Mentorship and Support: Serve as a mentor and resource for students, providing guidance on academic success, career pathways, and professional development. Address student concerns and collaborate with the Program Coordinator to support student retention and success. Equipment and Inventory Management: Assist in maintaining lab equipment and training materials, ensuring resources are available and in good condition for instructional use. Report equipment needs to the Program Coordinator for timely replenishment. Requirements: Associate Degree, or vocational or technical school degree Valid Drivers License Paramedic License and ACLS Instructor 1-3 years precious experience Working knowledge of Microsoft Office software Excellent written and verbal communication skills Benefits: Barry University offers a comprehensive benefits package to full-time employees that includes health, dental, vision, life insurance, retirement, tuition assistance, paid time off and work/life balance initiatives such as wellness programs, spirituality in the workplace, and training and development. Barry University is an Equal Opportunity Employer, committed to a diverse and inclusive work environment.

jobs.description: Current Employees: If you are a current Staff, Faculty or Temporary employee at the University of Miami, please click here to log in to Workday to use the internal application process. To learn how to apply for a faculty or staff position, please review this tip sheet . This individual will be a faculty member in the Department of Anesthesiology and will report directly to the Vice Chairman, or his designee. This individual will be an expert on translational development of Herpes Simplex Virus (HSV) based therapeutics for treating serious chronic neurological disorders. A focus on nonopioid chronic pain therapeutics research and therapeutic candidate development are highly preferred. The hiring rank will be based on experience and current/past level of research funding. The individual job description will include the following: Develop competitive research projects and design and submit timely competitive research-oriented grants and contracts to funding agencies. It is expected that the successful candidate will have a track record of obtaining research funding in scientific disciplines (clinical, basic sciences, or both) relevant to the Department and successfully obtain substantial research support for his/her own projects within three years. This individual will be an excellent communicator in writing and spoken English. Represent the Department at various international, national, state and local meetings, and make professional presentations to students, colleagues, support groups and community groups. Publish research findings in top refereed journals, book chapters, and books. The individual will work with faculty and staff to assist other investigators in their career development and obtain research funding within the Department and from other disciplines. Developing and teach relevant courses in the Department of Anesthesiology as assigned by the Department Chair, or their designee. Participating in the development and mentoring of residents, fellows, students and faculty in the capacity of advisor. Participate in external, institutional and Departmental committees. The Department of Anesthesiology is in need of a faculty member to work within the Division of Translational Research. The Division is engaged in interdisciplinary translational research programs spanning bench-to-bedside developing gene therapies for chronic neurological conditions with substantial ongoing NIH support. This position is open at the assistant/associate/full professor level. The appointment will depend on the candidates training and experience. This role requires the candidate to possess broad training in Herpes Simplex Virus (HSV) gene therapy, microbiology, physiology, pharmacology, molecular biology, as well as animal models of human disease. The incumbent will participate in ongoing gene therapy programs and carry out independent funded research projects. These projects should be relevant to translational development of HSV-based therapeutics for treating serious chronic neurological disorders in support of the Department’s long-term research mission. The successful candidate is expected to have extramural research funding and/or the ability to develop competitive research projects and design and submit timely competitive research-oriented grants and contracts to funding agencies. In addition, the candidate must be capable of participating in team science and interactions with multiple departments and institutions as well as train and support technicians, students, fellows, and faculty. This Faculty member will also mentor faculty, fellows, residents, and represent the Department at various national, state and local meetings, publish research findings, and develop and teach courses within the Department. The incumbent will have a PhD; and/or MD; and/or DVM with a minimum of 3+ years of relevant professional experience. The University of Miami is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Applicants and employees are protected from discrimination base

To learn how to apply for a faculty or staff position, please review this tip sheet . About the Department The Dr. John T. Macdonald Foundation Department of Human Genetics at the University of Miami Miller School of Medicine is a nationally recognized center for clinical genetics, genomic research, and medical education. The Department houses the Medical Genetics Residency Program, the South Florida Newborn Screening Program, and a broad research portfolio spanning genetic disorders, neurogenetics, and inborn errors of metabolism. Faculty provide clinical care through University of Miami Hospital and Clinics/ UHealth and Jackson Memorial Hospital, serving a large and diverse South Florida patient population. Position Summary The Department seeks a board-certified (or board-eligible) Clinical Geneticist to join our Division of Clinical and Translational Genetics, with a clinical and academic focus on inborn errors of metabolism and metabolic genetic disease. This faculty member will help lead metabolic patient care alongside our existing metabolic genetics team, manage a mixed pediatric and adult caseload, and contribute to resident education, newborn screening follow-up, and clinical research. This role is modeled on the scope of practice of our current faculty, including responsibility for a substantial portion of the Department's metabolic genetics patients, and offers the opportunity to build a clinical and academic niche within an established, highly collaborative division. Key Responsibilities Provide outpatient and inpatient clinical genetics consultation, with an emphasis on but not limite d to inborn errors of metabolism (e.g., lysosomal storage disorders, galactosemia, urea cycle disorders, and related conditions) across the pediatric-to-adult lifespan Evaluate, diagnose, and manage patients referred through the Newborn Screening Program, coordinating follow-up testing and long-term management Participate in multidisciplinary clinics and collaborate with specialists in general and specialty genetics clinics and metabolism, biochemical genetics, dietetics/nutrition, neurology, and related fields Order and interpret molecular and biochemical diagnostic testing, and provide treat ment, prevention, genetic counseling , and family risk assessment Contribute to teaching and supervision within the Medical Genetics Residency Program, including didactics, case conferences, and bedside/clinic teaching Engage in clinical or translational research, with opportunities to contribute to ongoing studies in rare disease diagnosis (e.g., Undiagnosed Diseases Network-type work) and publish in peer-reviewed journals Participate in departmental committees, quality initiatives, and community/professional education as needed Qualifications Required: M.D. degree Board certification (or eligibility) in Clinical Genetics through the American Board of Medical Genetics and Genomics (ABMGG), or equivalent Eligible for medical licensure in the State of Florida Strong clinical, communication, and interpersonal skills for working with patients, families, and multidisciplinary teams Preferred: Additional training in Pediatrics, Internal Medicine, or Clinical Biochemical Genetics Prior clinical experience managing genetic disorders including inborn errors of metabolism or biochemical genetic disorders Experience with newborn screening follow-up and long-term metabolic disease management Demonstrated interest or experience in resident/fellow teaching Record of scholarly activity (publications, abstracts, presentations) Academic Appointment Appointment rank (Clinical Assistant Professor, Clinical Associate Professor, or higher) will be commensurate with experience, within the Division of Clinical and Translational Genetics, Department of Human Genetics, University of Mia

The University of Miami Leonard Miller School of Medicine The University of Miami Leonard Miller School of Medicine (MSOM) is the oldest medical school in Florida. Headquartered in downtown Miami, the medical campus provides a full range of inpatient, outpatient, and surgical services, with 1,200 physicians and scientists. Additional facilities extent into Palm Beach, Broward, and Collier Counties, and include the University of Miami Hospital, Bascom Palmer Eye Institute, Sylvester Comprehensive Cancer Center, and Lennar Foundation Medical Center. The MSOM is affiliated with Jackson Health System (JHS), several hospitals, one of the largest public-health systems in the US, and Miami VA System. MSOM offers leading programs in transplantation, cancer care, ophthalmology, neurosciences, and genomics, including outstanding pediatric programs in all areas. With more than 2,000 active research projects and $260 million in private and public funding, MSOM ranks among the top 40 NIH-funded medical schools. Core services and research support structures are provided, as well as mentoring, education and consultation through the Miami Clinical Translational Science Institute. Department of Pediatrics The MSOM Department of Pediatrics consists of 150 faculty and 440 staff, caring for patients from South Florida, across the entire state, and throughout the US, as well as from Latin America and the Caribbean, through the University of Miami Medical Group and JHS. The Department’s mission is accomplishing extraordinary things every day for children of all ages. The Department staffs three hospitals – the 225-bed Holtz Children’s Hospital and two community hospitals; it also provides care at nine ambulatory sites. Community outreach is accomplished through the Pediatric Mobile Clinic, 36 school clinic sites, and the Injury Free Mobile Unit. The Department operates the Debbie School, a 150-student early child-care facility focused on children with special needs and special-education training. In addition, the South Florida Poison Control Center and the Child Protection Team are part of the Department. The Batchelor Children’s Research Institute and Mailman Center for Child Development house research and clinical activities. Department faculty are responsible for the education of 200 medical students (both MD and combined MD/MPH); 72 categorical pediatric residents; 20 med/peds residents; 41 fellows in 10 subspecialties; masters, doctoral and post-doctoral students in child psychology; and several other ancillary areas. Research advancement is augmented by the annual Micah Batchelor Awards, which distributes $500,000 in intramural grants annually. Summary The Chief of the Division of Pediatric Nephrology is responsible for coordinating the Division's clinical, research, and educational activities by providing administrative direction, in collaboration with the Department's Chair and SAO, and hospital's administration. This position is also responsible for the strategic clinical relationships with physicians across MSOM and Holtz Children's Hospital, as well as those with the nursing staff, pharmacy, laboratories, and technical staff. The Chief will ensure adherence of pediatric nephrologist with all service-line rules and regulations regarding clinical patient care, billing documentation, and HIPAA, and will participate in the development and leadership of quality and safety initiatives and clinical practice improvements. Schmidt College of Medicine at Florida Atlantic University in their search for the next Associate Dean for Medial Education, a key faculty leadership role overseeing undergraduate medical education, including curriculum, assessment, accreditation, and educational innovation. Florida Atlantic University (Florida Atlantic) is a public research university with ten colleges, 30,000 students, and six campuses spanning more than 100 miles of coastline. The University has seen remarkable growth in its programs and reputation in just the last few years, including doubling research expenditures, enrolling an all-time high number of National Merit Scholars, setting new records for private gifts to the FAU Foundation, increasing graduation and academic progress rates, and raising the profile of Florida Atlantic's athletics program. For the first time in 2026, Florida Atlantic was named a "Top 100 Public University" by U.S. News & World Report , rising from No. 103 in last year’s ranking of the nation’s best universities. Five local hospitals from top healthcare systems in the region, namely Baptist Health and Tenet Health, serve as key partners in undergraduate medical education (UME) and form the Graduate Medical Education (GME) Consortium, which offers residency and fellowship programs. The College is also affiliated with Cleveland Clinic Florida, HCA, and local behavioral health medical centers. The College also has a faculty practice plan, Florida Atlantic Medical Group, and is home to the Max Planck Florida Institute for Neuroscience, offering outstanding research and educational opportunities for faculty and students. The College annually provides approximately 400 students with a variety of educational offerings, including an M.D. program, an M.D./Ph.D. program, M.S. and Ph.D. degree programs in Biomedical Sciences, and graduate certificates. This highly visible leader will guide the continued evolution of an innovative, learner-centered curriculum, ensuring seamless integration across the pre-clinical and clinical years while advancing emerging areas of medical education such as health systems science, artificial intelligence, nutrition, and point-of-care ultrasound. The Associate Dean will oversee curriculum quality, assessment, accreditation readiness, and continuous quality improvement efforts; mentor and support course and clerkship directors; and foster collaboration among faculty, academic leaders, and community-based clinical partners. The successful candidate will bring the vision, innovation, and relationship-building skills necessary to support the College's long-term growth, enhance educational excellence, and prepare the medical education enterprise for future expansion. Job Description: The Department of Clinical and Health Psychology (CHP) within the College of Public Health and Health Professions at the University of Florida is recruiting for three faculty positions in clinical health psychology at the Assistant or Associate Professor level. These are full-time (1.0 FTE), 12-month tenure-track positions; preference is at the Associate Professor rank, but applicants at the Assistant Professor rank are welcome. We are seeking psychologists with research and clinical interests in health psychology. We welcome all subspecialties; however, established collaborations with UF Health include solid organ transplant, psycho-oncology, pain and chronic illness, weight management, and/or sleep. The ideal candidates for these positions are expected to display a strong career record of scientific and scholarly achievements relative to other professionals at their current professional rank; have active interest and skills in building a collaborative research program within a dynamic, interprofessional, academic health center environment; add depth and/or breadth to existing areas of specialization represented by existing faculty in the Medical/Health Psychology area; and possess competency and willingness to engage in (i) mentorship of research and (ii) supervision of behavioral health service delivery within a Scientist-Practitioner graduate training program emphasizing evidence-based practice. The Candidates will work closely with colleagues within the department, physicians, and other healthcare providers in a dynamic healthcare environment. If applicable, day-to-day clinical service delivery responsibilities may take place across a variety of settings within the UF Health Science Center, including our outpatient UF Psychology Specialties Clinic, other UF Health Outpatient Clinics, or the inpatient units at UF Health/Shands Hospital. Taking into account interest and departmental needs, the faculty members will be expected to participate in clinical coverage for other departments' faculty as needed. In addition, classroom teaching may be assigned as part of the faculty member’s responsibilities. The Department (http://chp.phhp.ufl.edu): CHP manages a unique, freestanding academic clinical psychology program with 38 core faculty, more than 60 doctoral students, over 10 Interns, and multiple Postdoctoral Fellows. CHP has APA-accredited clinical psychology PhD and Internship programs. The Department has a 50-year history of providing APA-accredited training in clinical psychology and advanced specialty-specific training in three concentration areas: Clinical Health Psychology, Clinical Child/Pediatric Psychology, and Neuropsychology. The doctoral program has been ranked in the 93rd percentile by the National Research Council’s data-based ranking system. jobs.description: Business Organizational Leadership Department Associate Professor of Business Organizational Leadership Position Overview Title Department Chair & Associate Professor of Business Organizational Leadership Department Business Organizational Leadership Department Reports to Vice President for Academic Affairs Location Trinity College of Florida (Trinity, FL — On-site) Contract Period July 1 – June 30 (Annual Contract) Compensation Competitive salary commensurate with experience/rank (includes medical insurance, term life insurance policy, and 401(k) retirement plan; moving expense reimbursement assistance available) Position Summary Trinity College of Florida seeks an experienced, biblically grounded academic leader to serve as Department Chair and Faculty Member in the Business Organizational Leadership Department. This role combines full-time classroom teaching, curriculum design, program assessment, faculty development, and departmental leadership. The Chair serves as the primary steward of the Business Organizational Leadership curriculum, ensuring academic excellence, strategic workforce relevance, and integration of a Christian worldview across all organizational leadership courses. Key Responsibilities 1. Departmental Administration & Leadership Curriculum Design & Innovation: Initiate and oversee course and curricular design, continuous program reviews, and enhancements within the Business Organizational Leadership Department to align with academic and marketplace standards. Assessment & Planning: Conduct annual assessment and strategic planning for departmental improvement; compile and present findings and action plans to the Assessment and Planning Committee. Teach-Out & Articulation Assistance: Assist in developing teach-out plans and articulation agreements for incoming transfer students from closing or partnering institutions. Budget & Operations: Oversee departmental budgeting, planning, and academic policy reviews in alignment with institutional priorities. 2. Teaching & Academic Advising Instructional Load: Teach 12 to 18 credit hours per semester across traditional day, in-seat, and/or online formats within the Business Organizational Leadership discipline. Academic Advising & Consulting: Provide academic consulting and course planning to the Director of Student Success and deliver direct academic advising and mentoring to students majoring in Business Organizational Leadership. Academic Freedom: Exercise academic freedom in accordance with the college’s Faculty Handbook and Statement of Faith. 3. Faculty Recruitment, Vetting & Evaluation Faculty Search & Hiring: Collaborate with the Vice President for Academic Affairs and the President in identifying personnel needs, vetting credentials, and interviewing candidates for full-time and adjunct faculty appointments within the department. Adjunct Faculty Supervision & Evaluation: Conduct annual evaluations of adjunct business instructors with 5 years or less of teaching experience, and biannual evaluations of adjunct instructors with over 5 years of teaching experience. Classroom Observations: Participate in candidate campus interviews, evaluating sample teaching sessions and professional experience in management and organizational leadership. 4. Campus Engagement, Committees & Spiritual Mentorship Governance: Actively serve on appointed faculty and institutional committees governing the academic and administrative affairs of the college. Student Discipleship: Actively develop discipleship relationships with students and facilitate/lead a weekly student small group or ministry cohort. College Representation: Articulate and represent the vision of Trinity College of Florida positively to students, staff, alumni, local churches, and professional/business networks. Qualifications & Requirements Required Education & Academic Credentials Terminal Degree Preferred: An earned academic doctorate (Ph.D., D.B.A., Ed.D., or related terminal degree) in Business Administration,

The University of Miami, Miller School of Medicine, is seeking an experienced and academically driven Associate Professor of Cardiology to join our dynamic Heart Failure and Transplant team. This position offers an exciting opportunity to work in a collaborative, patient-centered environment focused on the comprehensive management of advanced heart failure, mechanical circulatory support, and cardiac transplantation. Clinical Responsibilities: Provide specialized outpatient and inpatient care for patients with advanced heart failure, including those requiring mechanical circulatory support (LVAD) and heart transplantation. Manage complex heart failure cases, including evaluation and optimization of guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT). Participate in the evaluation and selection of candidates for advanced therapies, including transplant and durable mechanical support. Collaborate closely with a multidisciplinary team including cardiothoracic surgery, transplant coordinators, intensivists, and other subspecialties. Support post-transplant and LVAD patient management, including longitudinal follow-up and complication management. Academic and Leadership Responsibilities: Participate in clinical research initiatives in heart failure, mechanical circulatory support, and transplantation, with expectation of scholarly productivity. Teach and mentor medical students, residents, fellows, and junior faculty within the cardiovascular division. Contribute to the advancement of the Heart Failure and Transplant program through innovation, quality improvement, and program development. Provide leadership in multidisciplinary team initiatives and support institutional priorities in high-acuity cardiovascular care. Maintain up-to-date knowledge of advances in heart failure therapies and integrate evidence-based practices into clinical care. Qualifications: MD or DO degree with board certification in Cardiovascular Disease ; board certification/eligibility in Advanced Heart Failure and Transplant Cardiology preferred. Completion of fellowship training in Cardiovascular Disease and Advanced Heart Failure/Transplant Cardiology. Demonstrated experience in the management of advanced heart failure, transplant patients, and mechanical circulatory support. Established academic track record appropriate for appointment at the Associate Professor level. Strong clinical, teaching, and collaborative skills within a multidisciplinary environment. The Clinical Assistant/Associate Professor position is critical to maintaining the quality and continuity of the Psychiatric Mental Health Nursing (PMHNP) program. Position Summary The Transplant Hepatologist provides comprehensive care to patients with acute and chronic liver disease and to liver transplant recipients across the full continuum of care — candidate evaluation, waitlist management, perioperative care, and long-term post-transplant follow-up. The physician serves as an integral member of a multidisciplinary transplant team and contributes to clinical excellence, program growth, education, and research. Essential Duties and Responsibilities Evaluate patients with end-stage liver disease and acute liver failure for transplant candidacy and present cases to the multidisciplinary selection committee. Manage waitlisted patients, including MELD-based prioritization and optimization of medical status. Manage complications of cirrhosis and portal hypertension, including ascites, variceal bleeding, hepatic encephalopathy, and hepatocellular carcinoma. Direct post-transplant medical management, including immunosuppression, prophylaxis, and treatment of infectious, biliary, and vascular complications. Diagnose and manage acute and chronic allograft rejection and recurrent liver disease. Perform and/or interpret relevant procedures and diagnostics (e.g., paracentesis, liver biopsy interpretation, endoscopic evaluation and management of varices as applicable). Participate in a shared inpatient and on-call rotation for the transplant service. Collaborate with transplant surgery, hepatobiliary and oncology specialists, coordinators, pharmacists, and allied health. Contribute to quality assurance, regulatory compliance, and outcomes reporting (UNOS/OPTN, CMS). Support clinical research and teaching of residents, fellows, and advanced practice providers. Required Qualifications MD or DO degree. Board certification or board eligibility in Internal Medicine and Gastroenterology by the ABIM. Board certification or eligibility in Transplant Hepatology (or completion of an accredited Transplant Hepatology fellowship or equivalent training). Active, unrestricted FL medical license (or eligibility) and DEA registration. Eligibility for medical staff privileges at University of Miami and Jackson Memorial Hospital Preferred Qualifications Dedicated transplant hepatology fellowship. Experience within an established liver transplant program, including living donor transplantation. Record of scholarly activity, clinical trials, or funded research. Knowledge, Skills & Abilities Expertise in immunosuppression management and transplant hepatology. Strong skills in managing decompensated cirrhosis and its complications. Excellent communication and collaboration skills within a multidisciplinary team. Commitment to patient safety, quality outcomes, and regulatory standards. Physical Requirements & Work Environment Clinical hospital and outpatient environment; ability to perform/assist procedures and respond to urgent clinical needs. Ability to meet the physical demands of patient care. The University of Miami is an Equal Opportunity Employer. The primary appointment can be in the Department of Chemical, Environmental and Materials Engineering, which houses ongoing work in material synthesis, catalysis and energy storage, or in the Department of Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering, which houses ongoing work in advanced additive manufacturing of polymer composites, multifunctional ceramics, and metallic laser powder bed fusion. jobs.title: ESL Instructor
jobs.description: Department English Language Program-OPS Compensation $30.00 Hourly Job Responsibilities The English Language Program accepts applications on an ongoing basis to maintain a pool of qualified ESL instructors. Instructors are hired as teaching needs arise based on student enrollment, program needs, and instructor availability. Applicants may be contacted when teaching opportunities become available. Employment is offered on a semester-by-semester basis. Job Functions An ESL Instructor provides English language instruction to multilingual and international students at the University of North Florida’s English Language Program. Students come from a variety of countries and linguistic backgrounds and study English for a range of goals, including preparing for university admission and advancing their professional lives. The English Language Program offers six proficiency levels: Beginning 00, High-Beginning 10, Intermediate 20, High-Intermediate 30, Advanced 40, and Pre-University 50. Courses focus primarily on general and academic English, with instruction in reading/writing, listening/speaking/vocabulary, and grammar. The ESL Instructor position is a part-time, in-person position in our Day Program. The Day Program operates Monday–Thursday, 9:00 a.m.–3:00 p.m., for three semesters per year: spring, summer, and fall. A full teaching schedule is 3 classes per day, approximately 26 hours per week. Reduced schedules of 1–2 classes per day may also be available. Instructors indicate their availability when scheduling, and semester assignments are made based on instructor availability, enrollment, and program needs. ESL Instructors are assigned specific courses each semester but should be prepared to teach across subject areas and proficiency levels as program needs require. Required Qualifications •Bachelor's degree in English, TESOL, Applied Linguistics, Second Language Acquisition, English Education, or a related field. •Experience teaching English to multilingual learners from diverse linguistic and cultural backgrounds. •Knowledge and experience teaching academic English. •Ability to manage a classroom effectively and create an engaging learning environment. Fellows will gain experience in interpreting and performing imaging studies to enhance diagnostic and therapeutic decision-making for complex cardiovascular patients. Responsibilities: Clinical Training : Participate in daily clinical practice with a multidisciplinary team, interpreting advanced cardiovascular imaging modalities including cardiac CT, MRI, echocardiography, and nuclear imaging. Advanced Imaging Techniques : Obtain expertise in advanced techniques such as myocardial perfusion imaging, coronary artery imaging, cardiac function evaluation, and tissue characterization using state-of-the-art imaging modalities. Research Opportunities : Engage in clinical and translational research projects related to cardiovascular imaging. Fellows will have the opportunity to collaborate with faculty on ongoing studies and contribute to publications in high-impact journals. Collaboration with Specialists : Work closely with cardiologists, radiologists, and other specialists to develop integrated treatment strategies for patients with complex cardiovascular conditions. Educational Activities : Participate in didactic teaching sessions, case discussions, and regular departmental conferences. Fellows will also be encouraged to present at local and national meetings. Quality Assurance and Protocol Development : Gain experience in quality assurance processes and protocol development to ensure accurate imaging results and effective clinical utilization. Qualifications: Education : MD or equivalent degree. Completion of an ACGME-accredited residency in Internal Medicine, Cardiology, Radiology, or other relevant specialty. Experience : Previous experience in cardiovascular imaging is highly preferred, though motivated applicants with strong backgrounds in cardiology or radiology will be considered. Licensure : Must be eligible for licensure in the state of Florida. Skills : Strong analytical, communication, and organizational skills. Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced, multidisciplinary environment. Research Interest : Interest in cardiovascular imaging research and its clinical applications. Compensation : Competitive stipend based on experience. Health Insurance : Comprehensive health, dental, and vision insurance coverage. Academic Development : Opportunities to engage in high-quality research and contribute to academic publications. Professional Networking : Exposure to a diverse clinical and research network, with opportunities to collaborate with leading experts in the field of cardiovascular imaging. We are interested in candidates who wish to be part of a transformative cancer control research program and have research interests and expertise in cancer prevention, lifestyle medicine and survivorship. There is particular interest in candidates who are team scientists, highly collaborative and have expertise in one or more of the following areas: exercise and physical activity; nutrition; obesity and body composition; symptom and toxicities measurement and management; patient reported outcomes (PROs); technology-supported behavioral interventions; biobehavioral mechanisms in cancer control; electronic health record (EHR), bioinformatics and value-based models of cancer survivorship care; health disparities in specific survivorship subgroups (e.g., LGBT; Hispanics; Elderly); cardiometabolic health in cancer survivors; and/or translational science and dissemination and implementation research. Responsibilities: - Conduct independent and NIH and VA funded research in the field of epigenetics and molecular biology with a focus on HIV infection, drugs use, cardiology and Alzheimer’s Disease (AD). - Design and perform experiments to investigate molecular pathways involved in cardiovascular diseases (AD). - Analyze and interpret research data using a variety of molecular biology techniques, including PCR, gel electrophoresis, Western blotting, and immunohistochemistry. - Collaborate with other researchers and scientists to develop and execute research projects. - Publish research findings in peer-reviewed scientific journals and present research at conferences and meetings. - Assist in the preparation of grant proposals to secure funding for research projects. - Applicants are also encouraged to develop his/her own research proposals - Supervise and mentor postdocs and research assistants in the laboratory. - Stay up-to-date with the latest advancements in molecular biology and cardiology research. We offer a competitive salary and benefits package, as well as a supportive and collaborative research environment. This is an excellent opportunity for a talented and ambitious researcher to contribute to cutting-edge molecular biology research in the field of cardiology. To learn how to apply for a faculty or staff position, please review this tip sheet . Miami is rapidly emerging as a leading global hub for innovation and technology. As the seventh-largest metro area in the United States and one of the fastest-growing cities, Miami continues to attract top talent and investment, particularly in the fields of Technology, FinTech, Artificial Intelligence, and Healthcare. With its unique combination of cultural diversity, entrepreneurial spirit, no state income taxes, and favorable climate, Miami is drawing a massive influx of wealth and expertise from around the world. The city is positioning itself as a center for cutting-edge developments in financial technology, healthcare analytics, life sciences, green technology, and digital transformation. We are one of the largest private employers in Miami, home to more than 16,000 faculty and staff from across the globe. The Miami Herbert Business School (MHBS) at the University of Miami plans to appoint four tenured or tenure-track faculty members in business and management, with a specific focus on attracting top talent in strategic areas of differentiation, such as Finance, Artificial Intelligence, Business Analytics, Healthcare, Innovation, Entrepreneurship, and Sustainability. Boundary spanning scholars who can work in multiple strategic areas are preferred. Help us achieve our goal of engaging with Miami’s rapidly growing finance, technology, entrepreneurship, and innovation community. POSITION SUMMARY The Surgical Director of the Living Donor Liver Transplant (LDLT) Program provides strategic, clinical, and operational leadership for all aspects of living donor liver transplantation. This senior faculty position carries ultimate responsibility for donor safety, recipient outcomes, program integrity, and regulatory compliance. The Surgical Director collaborates closely with the Hepatology Director, transplant coordinators, anesthesia, critical care, and administrative leadership to drive a nationally recognized, high-volume program. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES Clinical Leadership & Surgical Care Perform complex living donor hepatectomies (right lobe, left lobe, left lateral segment) and recipient implantations, including technically demanding redo transplants and combined organ procedures. Serve as the primary attending surgeon of record for all living donor operations and maintain active operative involvement in recipient surgeries. Ensure the highest standards of peri-operative donor and recipient care, including ICU management, post-operative follow-up, and long-term surveillance. Provide 24/7 availability and back-up coverage for on-call transplant surgical emergencies. Program Development & Strategy Define and execute the strategic vision for program growth, including expansion of donor and recipient volumes, geographic referral development, and new surgical techniques (e.g., laparoscopic/robotic donor hepatectomy). Establish and monitor key performance indicators (KPIs) including donor morbidity/mortality, recipient graft survival, length of stay, and readmission rates. Identify and implement quality improvement initiatives aligned with SRTR benchmarking data and ASTS best practice guidelines. Lead multidisciplinary case conferences (selection committee, M&M, QI committee) and foster a culture of safety and continuous improvement. Regulatory Compliance & Accreditation Serve as the designated Transplant Program Director (or co-Director) with UNOS/OPTN, ensuring the program meets all certification requirements and key personnel qualifications. Oversee adherence to MPSC performance metrics and respond to any MPSC reviews or variance reports in collaboration with hospital leadership. Maintain familiarity with CMS Conditions of Participation for transplant programs and ensure timely data submission and policy compliance. Lead preparation for JCAHO and other accreditation site visits related to transplant services. Donor Evaluation & Selection Chair or co- chair the Living Donor Selection Committee, ensuring rigorous, ethical, and evidence-based donor evaluation independent of recipient pressures. Standardize donor evaluation pathways, consent processes, and psychosocial screening protocols in accordance with ASTS, AST, and AASLD guidelines. Oversee the long-term follow-up and reporting of living donors per OPTN Policy 18. Serve as a resource and advocate for potential donors, ensuring informed consent is comprehensive and free of coercion. Design and deliver didactic curriculum for the transplant surgery fellowship aligned with ASTS training standards. Pursue an active scholarly agenda including peer-reviewed publications, national conference presentations, and clinical or translational research. Participate in grant development related to living donor transplantation, outcomes research, or surgical innovation. Open-Rank Tenure-Track/Tenured Faculty Positions in Electrical and Computer Engineering College of Engineering, University of Miami The Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering (ECE) at the University of Miami (Coral Gables, FL) invites nominations and applications for three open-rank, tenure-track faculty positions as part of a bold growth trajectory that will significantly expand the department’s impact and visibility. This search represents the first phase of a multi-phase hiring plan to be executed over the next three to four years. While applications are welcome at all ranks, the department is particularly interested in early and mid-career faculty who are ready to accelerate UM ECE’s growth with established research programs. We seek exceptional scholars in the following strategic thrust areas : AI-Powered Microchips and Systems (AI-powered microchips, AI-powered medical systems, edge intelligence, trustworthy and explainable AI) Robotics and Autonomous Systems (medical and surgical robotics, autonomous vehicles, drones, human–machine collaboration, assistive systems) Quantum and Nano Technologies (quantum communication, computing, sensing, nanoelectronics, emerging devices, energy-efficient systems) Cybersecurity and Cyber Physical Systems (hardware, software, and network security; AI for secure and resilient systems; privacy; secure sensing and control in critical infrastructures) Candidates with a PhD in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or other closely related engineering disciplines are encouraged to apply. Faculty will also have opportunities to collaborate with the Rosenstiel School of Marine, Atmospheric, and Earth Science (RSMAS), one of the nation’s top-ranked marine and atmospheric research schools, expanding the potential for innovation in areas such as sensing, climate, and ocean technologies. jobs.description: Postdoctoral Associate Apply now Job no: 541548 Work type: Post Doc Associate Location: Main Campus (Gainesville, FL) Categories: Biology/Life Science, Engineering, Physical/Mathematical Sciences Department:19340000 - EG-BIOMEDICAL ENGINEERING Classification Title: Postdoctoral Associate Classification Minimum Requirements: Applicants are expected to have a Ph.D. in a field such as veterinary sciences, biomedical sciences, engineering, or neuroscience. Other degree fields will also be considered if the applicant has skill sets that complement our research team. Applicants must have experience with manuscript preparation and submission and must be comfortable working with large animals (training will be provided upon hire). Applicants must also demonstrate the ability and willingness to mentor and manage graduate students. Experience with grant writing and prior formal mentoring of students is desirable. Job Description: The Orthopaedic Biomedical Engineering (OrthoBME) Laboratory is seeking a post-doctoral fellow to help lead an observational clinical study on osteoarthritic pain in veterinary equine populations. Osteoarthritis (OA) is common in horses, and like human OA, equine OA is often idiopathic, develops over years, and shows a poor match between the severity of joint damage and the severity of symptoms. These parallels make naturally-occurring equine OA a powerful population for developing pain measures that can translate to humans. As such, our study is being conducted entirely in privately-owned equine patients with naturally occurring fetlock OA, where the overall goal of the study is to determine the best and most reliable measures of naturally-occurring OA pain in horses. Following enrollment visits conducted by the UF College of Veterinary Medicine, our assessment team travels to the equine patient (farms and ranches near Gainesville) and then performs on-site measurements of neural processing, autonomic nervous system function, activity, and gait mechanics, among other physiologic tests. We are seeking a post-doctoral fellow to join this NIH-funded project, helping our team establish reliable and valid behavioral measures of OA pain in horses. Using psychometric statistical approaches, our team will then evaluate the reliability and validity of these measures and compare them with data from ongoing human OA pain studies at the UF Pain Research and Intervention Center of Excellence. Again, testing is conducted at the horses' housing sites in the Gainesville-Ocala area, in partnership with the UF College of Veterinary Medicine. The OrthoBME lab is focused on understanding how chronic joint degeneration leads to chronic pain and disability. To achieve this goal, our team works with samples and data collected from rodent models, large animal veterinary patients, and human patients (www.orthobme.com). A key tenet of our laboratory environment is team-based science. We feature a highly collaborative environment and often take on ambitious projects that integrate the skills and abilities of multiple scientific fields. As such, strong communication skills, willingness to learn, and the ability to work with and mentor others are highly important for all members of our team. The post-doctoral fellow will serve as a day-to-day scientific leader for this project and will work closely with a team of graduate students. Responsibilities will include coordinating study activities and timelines, mentoring graduate students in data collection and analysis, supporting the training and calibration of study personnel, and helping maintain data quality and protocol standardization. Ideally, the post-doctoral fellow will also lead the quantitative sensory testing (QST) portion of the project, adapting human QST protocols to the horse. Prior experience with QST is not required; training will be provided. Job Description: The Karst laboratory in the Department of Molecular Genetics and Microbiology at the University of Florida College of Medicine is seeking a highly motivated postdoctoral associate to join a newly funded NIH R01 project investigating how the early-life environment programs long-term metabolic health. Our laboratory recently discovered that maternal bile acids delivered during lactation act as developmental signals that regulate neonatal growth through the bile acid receptor TGR5. Remarkably, transient manipulation of this pathway during lactation has lasting consequences: offspring exposed to reduced maternal milk bile acids are protected from diet-induced obesity, insulin resistance, hyperinsulinemia, and fatty liver in adulthood. The successful candidate will investigate the cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying this developmental programming. Current studies focus on how bile acid signaling during early postnatal life establishes adipose tissue architecture and function, including effects on adipocyte progenitor populations and their developmental trajectories. Approaches will include mouse models, flow cytometry and cell sorting, lineage tracing, metabolic phenotyping, and single-cell genomic and epigenomic approaches. This is a new and rapidly developing research direction in the laboratory, providing substantial opportunity for the successful candidate to contribute intellectually to the project, develop independent questions, and shape its future direction. We are looking for a scientist who is curious, rigorous, collaborative, and interested in understanding how transient exposures during critical developmental windows can produce lifelong changes in physiology and disease susceptibility. jobs.description: Postdoctoral Scholar in Natural Language Processing and Mammalian Evolution Apply now Job no: 541480 Work type: Post Doc Associate Location: Main Campus (Gainesville, FL) Categories: Biology/Life Science, Education/Training/Instructional Design, Grant or Research Administration Department:56021500 - NH-MAMMALS Classification Title: Postdoctoral Scholar in Natural Language Processing and Mammalian Evolution Classification Minimum Requirements: Ph.D. in natural language processing, computer science, data science, ecology, evolutionary biology, biodiversity informatics, bioinformatics, or a closely related field, completed or expected to be completed before the start date. Job Description: Centuries of field observations, dietary studies, and taxonomic accounts contain an extraordinary amount of information about what mammals eat. However, these data remain embedded in unstructured text, scattered across thousands of publications, and are reported using inconsistent terminology and formats. This project seeks to unlock these hidden data by developing a human-in-the-loop AI pipeline that uses LLMs to read scientific literature at scale, extract consumer-food relationships, and convert qualitative descriptions into standardized ordinal dietary rankings suitable for evolutionary biology research. Our central hypothesis is that the published literature contains a vast reservoir of latent dietary information that can be systematically transformed into reproducible quantitative datasets. Existing mammalian diet databases rely heavily on manual expert curation, limiting their scope and scalability. By combining AI-assisted information extraction with expert validation, this project will create high-resolution dietary datasets spanning the mammalian tree at a scale that would be impractical through manual curation alone. The Postdoctoral Researcher will play a leading role in developing the dietary ranking framework and constructing the resulting database. Working closely with an interdisciplinary team of ecologists, biodiversity scientists, and AI researchers, the successful candidate will contribute to the development and evaluation of LLM-based information extraction methods, analyze large-scale dietary datasets, and help advance computational approaches for ecological synthesis. The Postdoctoral Researcher will conduct independent and collaborative research, publish in leading scientific journals, contribute to grant proposals, mentor graduate and undergraduate students, and help shape the future direction of this growing interdisciplinary research program. The project also provides excellent opportunities to develop expertise in AI for biodiversity science while building a strong publication record and collaborative network for an academic or research career.
