jobs.title: Postdoctoral Scholar, Daytona Beach Campus
jobs.description: Job Description The Opportunity Embry-Riddle Aeronautical University (ERAU), Daytona Beach Campus, invites applications for a full-time Postdoctoral Scholar position in the field of magnetospheric physics and space instrumentation. The successful candidate will contribute to cutting-edge research focused on the design and development of a miniature particle detector, as well as the analysis of satellite observations and numerical simulation results related to the Earth’s magnetosphere and space plasma environment. This position offers an exciting opportunity to work in a collaborative research environment at one of the world’s leading aerospace-focused universities. Position Responsibilities: Participate in the design, development, testing, and integration of a miniature particle detector for space applications. Analyze satellite measurements and numerical simulation results in the field of magnetospheric physics and space plasma science. Contribute to the development of data analysis tools and scientific interpretation of observational and modeling results. Prepare manuscripts for publication in peer-reviewed journals and present research findings at scientific conferences. Assist with proposal development and contribute to externally funded research activities. Collaborate with faculty, students, and external research partners on interdisciplinary research initiatives. Mentoring and Career Development: This position includes a structured mentoring plan designed to support the professional growth of an early-career postdoctoral scientist and foster the development of independent research capabilities. Mentoring activities will include: Weekly one-on-one meetings focused on research progress, manuscript preparation, proposal development, and career planning. Regular group meetings to encourage collaboration, scientific communication, and presentation skills. Guidance in building a competitive research portfolio, securing external funding, leading research projects, and publishing high-impact research. Career development support will include: Periodic discussions to define long-term career goals and identify funding opportunities. Collaborative establishment of short- and medium-term milestones, including manuscript submissions and grant applications. Opportunities to take increasing ownership of research activities, including project leadership, collaboration management, and mentoring junior trainees. The overall goal of this mentoring framework is to support the successful transition of the postdoctoral scholar toward research independence and long-term career advancement. For a century, we have led innovation in STEM education, serving more than 30,000 students around the globe. Our cutting-edge programs in Applied Science, Aviation, Business, Technology, Engineering, Safety, Security, and Space empower the next generation of leaders to shape the future of flight, exploration, and discovery. jobs.description: Professor, Marine Mammal Science Print Professor, Marine Mammal Science Salary Negotiable Location Sarasota, Florida, United States Job Type Full-Time Job Number 00556 Division Marine Mammal Science Opening Date 11/10/2025 Description Benefits Description We invite applications for an open-rank, tenure-track position in Marine Mammal Science beginning in August 2026. We seek a collaborative colleague whose expertise falls in one of two areas:Research methods, data science, or statistics; orMarine mammal science, broadly defined.The successful candidate will play a central role in supporting and expanding our interdisciplinary, research-intensive two-year Master’s program. Examples of Duties Our current faculty are leaders in dolphin cognition and echolocation, manatee acoustics and conservation, and pinniped cognition and marine mammal neurobiology. We are seeking a fourth faculty member whose expertise complements and broadens these strengths, particularly in spatial ecology, GIS, genetics, or other areas that expand our research portfolio. Experience or strong interest in cross-disciplinary data analysis or advanced quantitative methods is especially welcome, though not required.The new faculty member will mentor 4–6 graduate students annually, teach core courses and electives aligned with their expertise, and contribute to our strong culture of individualized mentorship and hands-on research training. There are no undergraduate teaching requirements; however, faculty may engage with undergraduates through collaborative research and occasional cross-listed courses.Research productivity is central to this position. We welcome applicants at any career stage who bring either an emerging or well-established research agenda that complements or enhances our existing strengths.The Marine Mammal Science program is housed in a restored historic mansion estate on Sarasota Bay, separate from the main campus, with two dedicated buildings and direct dock access. These facilities foster focused scholarship and close faculty-student collaboration. Florida offers exceptional opportunities for marine mammal research across springs, estuaries, and Gulf ecosystems, with access to diverse species including manatees (in both wild and rehabilitation contexts), the long-studied Sarasota Bay bottlenose dolphin community, Gulf cetaceans, and pinnipeds through regional partnerships. The program maintains strong regional collaborations and long-term data resources, including the Sarasota Bay Listening Network, creating rich opportunities for integrative and applied research.We welcome applicants who are excited to help build and shape a dynamic graduate program within a collegial, energetic academic community committed to scientific excellence and student success.Application review begins March 31, 2026, and will continue on a rolling basis until the position is filled.About New CollegeNew College is driven by a mission to be the best liberal arts college in America. New College, the nationally recognized honors college of the State University System of Florida, is an innovative liberal arts institution where students learn how to think, not what to think.Founded in 1960, the College has garnered national acclaim for its rigorous academics as students chart their own academic course with the assistance of faculty advisors and written assessments are given instead of letter grades. Conducting research is an important part of the undergraduate curriculum at New College with each student having to complete a senior thesis to graduate.The New College campus sits on the scenic Sarasota Bay and directly adjacent to one of the fastest-growing airports in the nation. The region consistently ranks among the best for quality of life, featuring world-famous beaches, historic architecture, and iconic fine & performing arts institutions.How to applyInterested candidates should apply online. jobs.description: The School of Arts and Communication at Florida Institute of Technology seeks a Postdoctoral Research Associate as an active participant in the project “Cultivating Core Character through the General Education Core,” funded by Wake Forest University and the Lilly Endowment Inc. under co-PIs Lars Jones, Andrew Aberdein, and Heidi Hatfield Edwards. Beyond pursuing their own research agenda, the successful candidate will work under the supervision of project PIs and is expected to begin the 12-month annual position in January 2027 and continue through the end of the grant term in July 2029. Funds available for approved grant-related travel. Salary supplements may also be available. Specific responsibilities will include: · Teaching up to or the equivalent of two core undergraduate courses directly tied to our character education framework, ensuring pedagogical fidelity and integration with project goals. · Partnering with the PIs to support faculty and student virtue-education training, including workshops, mentoring, classroom sessions, and follow-up engagement. · Supporting the PIs in university-wide advocacy and outreach to other colleges as well as to the broader public. · Assisting the lead PI in designing and leading the biweekly character colloquium (topic selection, readings, integration with curriculum). · Attending weekly project team meetings. · Contributing to assessment planning, execution, and review to enable a rigorous evaluation of student and faculty outcomes. · Coordinating implementation and analysis of the project’s diagnostic framework, ensuring consistent data collection, interpretation, and integration across participating courses. · Collaborating on pedagogical scholarship tied to project activities and outputs, in addition to advancing their own research agenda. · Working with in-house support units, as well as student assistants, to help the PIs develop four Canvas LMS modules for scalable character education use in the University and beyond. Qualifications The successful candidate must have: · A PhD (either awarded or submitted and with defense formally scheduled) in a humanistic discipline, with a research specialization related to character education and/or virtue theory. · Demonstrated strong interest and ability in teaching. · Excellent communication, interpersonal, and organizational skills. · Ability to work both independently and as part of a team that must deal professionally with people at all levels. Preference will be given for those candidates who have applied character education experience and/or a substantive specialization in virtue theory, complemented by demonstrated pedagogical skill. The successful candidate will participate in implementing and expanding our program across the instructional, developmental, and scholarly domains rather than acting only as a pure research scholar. Job Description: The Whitney Laboratory for Marine Bioscience is the premier marine research institute at the University of Florida. We are in an exciting phase of growth and invite applications for a tenure-track faculty appointment at the Assistant or Associate Professor level in one of two broad areas: Technology-Driven Integrative Physiology — connecting molecular, cellular, neural, biomechanical or developmental mechanisms to organismal function, behavior, and environmental response; OR AI-Enabled Cell, Molecular, or Genomic Biology — building advanced AI, machine learning, and other computational approaches to address basic biological questions. This position is part of a multi-year investment in faculty hiring, infrastructure, and research innovation at the UF Whitney Lab. Our new $40 million research building (38,000 ft2) opened in Spring 2026 with state-of-the-art wet and dry labs, large temperature-controlled seawater mesocosms and aquaculture tank systems, and world-leading imaging capabilities within the Whitney Laboratory Center for Biological Imaging and Discovery. jobs.description: Job Description The Opportunity The Aeronautical Science Department in the College of Aviation (COA) at Embry-Riddle Aeronautical University—Daytona Beach invites applications for a Tenure-Track 9-month appointment at the rank of Assistant Professor. The qualified candidate will teach courses held in the Department of Aeronautical Science for both the Aeronautical Science and Aeronautics undergraduate degree programs. They will also demonstrate an active or promising research agenda in areas of study consistent with flight operations or other aviation related subjects. Excellence in teaching and the growth of a well-developed research portfolio are our top priority. Other priorities include service to the university and a strong commitment to student mentorship. The qualified candidate will have a broad base of knowledge and experience in the operation of large-transport category aircraft or high performance aircraft used in commercial aircraft transportation. Courseware may include requisite material based in large transport category flight operations, crew resource management, aviation safety, domestic and international navigation, aircraft systems, and other content areas brought forth through course/department expansion. jobs.description: Current Employees: If you are a current Staff, Faculty or Temporary employee at the University of Miami, please click here to log in to Workday to use the internal application process. To learn how to apply for a faculty or staff position using the Career worklet, please review this tip sheet . Research Assistant Professor Positions (Research Track) The Department of Biomedical Engineering (BME) in the University of Miami (UM) College of Engineering, the Desai Sethi Urology Institute and the Miami Project to cure paralysis at UM Health system have multiple exciting opportunities for Research Assistant Professors , with the earliest start date of June 01, 2024. These positions are sponsored by multiple NIH Research Grants and UM to continue long-term research projects in the laboratory of Prof. Yingchun Zhang. Zhang's research aims to achieve the long-term goal of advancing Precision Rehabilitation. This will be accomplished through the comprehensive and quantitative assessment of dynamic activation and interactions of the brain, muscles, and brain-to-muscle pathways, using a combination of multimodal neuroimaging, neuroengineering, and neuromodulation techniques. Current research is dedicated to the advancement of innovative technologies aimed at achieving quantitative and precise diagnosis, phenotyping, and personalized treatment for a variety of neurological, neurodegenerative, and neuromuscular conditions. These conditions encompass psychiatric disorders, Alzheimer's disease (AD), stroke, spinal cord injury, pelvic floor dysfunctions, as well as the resultant movement disorders and pain conditions. The Research Assistant Professor will primarily work with Prof. Zhang and will also be embedded in the multidisciplinary team of investigators from BME at UM, and scientists/clinicians from the Desai Sethi Urology Institute and the Miami Project to cure paralysis at UM Health system. The position provides faculty level salary support, benefits, and a platform for professional growth including grant writing. Position Description and Requirements: Multimodal neuroimaging and neuroengineering: Developing novel technologies in precision diagnosis, phenotyping and personalized treatment of movement disorders, neuromuscular diseases and pain including the chronic pelvic pain. Experience in surface and intracranial EEG, ECoG, EMG, and/or tACS is desirable. Multimodal neuroimaging and neuromodulation: Developing novel techniques in precision diagnosis, phenotyping and personalized treatment of psychiatric disorders and Alzheimer's disease. Experience in surface and intracranial EEG, ECoG NIRS, MRI, TMS and/or Transcranial Focused Ultrasound is desirable. Regenerative rehabilitation: Developing regenerative therapies to enhance reduced muscle mass, restore impaired muscle innervation and co,ordination in conjunction with rehabilitative interventions. Experience in tissue engineering, extracorporeal shock wave therapy, and endogenous stem cell activation is desirable. Outstanding candidates with a MS or PhD degree in biomedical engineering, electrical engineering or relevant field, and strong publication records in relevant journals and outstanding writing and oral communication skills are encouraged to apply. Postdoctoral research experience is preferred. Interested applicants should send a curriculum vitae, statement describing research accomplishments and future research goals, relevant reprints, and the names of three references to y.zhang@miami.edu . jobs.description: Summary: The College of Arts and Sciences is currently accepting applications for the position of Visiting Professor in the Clinical Mental Health Counseling (CMHC) program. This position will serve for one year as a core faculty member in the CMHC program. The position is a primary teaching role in the graduate CMHC program which includes teaching a 4-4 load in fall and spring terms. Opportunities to teach in the undergraduate psychology program may also be included. Applicants with research, clinical, supervision, advocacy, social justice, and substance abuse experiences will be considered strong candidates for this position. Job Description: Essential duties and responsibilities Teach courses in accordance with college guidelines Participate in the college's assessment program of student performance Timely response to student questions and concerns Timely submission of university reports and requirements, such as attendance, grades, and student progress reports Required knowledge, skills, and abilities Candidates must be proficient with using technology for instructional delivery, such as learning management systems (e.g. Canvas) and presentation software (e.g. PowerPoint) Candidates must have an appreciation of different learning styles to incorporate into their instructional delivery Candidates must have excellent written, verbal, and interpersonal skills Minimum qualifications Candidates must have graduated with a Ph.D. in Counseling, Counselor Education, or a Counselor Education and Supervision program; or have a related doctoral degree and have been employed as a faculty member in a counselor education training program for approximately one academic year.
